EDITORIAL & PALEOGRAPHIC CONVENTIONS:
  * Original Early New High German (Frühneuhochdeutsch) orthography, vocalic
    diacritics (ÿ, ü, ö, ä), consonant clusters (kh-, p-, cz, ß), capitalization,
    and punctuation are strictly preserved.
  * Line breaks and line numbers match the physical manuscript lineation.
  * End-of-line hyphenation is represented by '=' (matching the scribal double
    or single oblique hyphen).
  * Red-ink headings and inline rubrics are marked as {rubric: ...}.
  * Scribal deletions are marked {del: ...} and supralinear additions {add: ...}.
  * Alchemical, planetary, and apothecary symbols are rendered with their
    Unicode glyph followed by diplomatic expansion in brackets, e.g. ▽ [Wasser].
  * Every page, column, figure, flap state, and line is anchored to its exact
    Wellcome IIIF Canvas pixel bounding box (#xywh=x,y,w,h).

ALCHEMICAL, PLANETARY & APOTHECARY GLYPH KEY:
  ℞    (U+211E         ) = Recipe                     -> Nimm / Recipe (Take)
  ▽    (U+25BD         ) = Aqua / Wasser              -> Wasser (Water)

  🜔▽   (U+1F714 U+25BD ) = Aqua salis / Salzwasser    -> Salzwasser (Brine / Salt water)
  ꝑll̵ (U+A751 U+006C U+006C U+0335) = Pulvis / Pulver            -> Pulver (Powder — loop p/o with crossed double-l)
  ✗    (U+2717         ) = Calx / Kalk / Pulver       -> Kalk / gebranntes Pulver (Calcined powder / Lime)
  ⊡    (U+22A1         ) = Urina / Harn               -> Harn / Urin (Urine — square with central dot)
  ☉    (U+2609         ) = Sol / Sonne / Gold         -> Sonne / Gold (Sun / Gold)
  ☿    (U+263F         ) = Mercurius / Quecksilber    -> Quecksilber / Mercurius (Mercury)
  ♁    (U+2641         ) = Antimonium / Spießglas     -> Antimonium / Spießglas (Antimony)
  🜖    (U+1F716        ) = Vitriolum / Vitriol        -> Vitriol (Sulfate of iron/copper)
  🜘    (U+1F718        ) = Alumen / Alaun             -> Alaun (Alum — astringent potassium aluminum sulfate)
  🜕    (U+1F715        ) = Nitrum / Salpeter          -> Salpeter (Nitre / Potassium nitrate — circle bisected by vertical bar)
  ♄    (U+2644         ) = Saturnus / Blei            -> Blei / Saturnus (Lead — e.g. 🜔 ♄ Sal Saturni, Sachari ♄ = lead acetate)
  XXX  (U+0058x3       ) = Camphora / Kampfer         -> Kampfer (Camphor — scribal triple-X cipher in dental anodynes)
  △    (U+25B3         ) = Ignis / Feuer              -> Feuer (Fire)
  ℔    (U+2114         ) = Libra / Pfund              -> Pfund (Apothecary pound, ~12 oz)
  ℥    (U+2125         ) = Uncia / Unze               -> Unze (Apothecary ounce, 8 drachms)
  ℨ    (U+2128         ) = Drachma / Quintlein        -> Drachme / Quintlein (Apothecary drachm, 3 scruples)
  ℈    (U+2108         ) = Scrupulus / Skrupel        -> Skrupel (Apothecary scruple, 20 grains)

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0007.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0007.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5012 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0007.JP2#xywh=240,314,4537,6150 | Center Rule X=2656
Summary:      First extant text page of the Arzneibuch ([p. 29], recto preceding p. 30; pages 1–28 wanting). Written in double column within red rules with red rubrics. Contains iatrochemical and folk-medical recipes using eggshells (for urinary calculus, hemorrhage, proud flesh), chimney soot (for cancer and plague anthrax), and sourdough bread (pharmacological properties, maturing poultice, febrile headache, inflamed eyes, post-febrile halitosis, and sustaining life by the aroma of bread).
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

PAGE / FOLIO: 30 (verso) | IIIF Canvas #8 (b18775275_MS_990_0008.JP2)
Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0008.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0008.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5425 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0008.JP2#xywh=575,274,4582,6224 | Center Rule X=2776
Summary:      Page 30 (verso, numbered '30' in upper-left margin; first numbered page cited in Wellcome catalogue 'pages 30-790'). Contains recipes for colic (Grimen), stiffening of the nerves (Nerven Erstarrung), pleurisy (Seiden stechen), plague prophylaxis (Pöß), the folk pediatric 'heart-worm or goat-worm' tested via a live gudgeon fish bound to the navel (Gaiß Würm den khindern), joint-water discharge (Glidt Wasser), consumption (Dörsucht / Dörsichtigen), snail oil for wasted limbs (Schwinden der glider), cough and hemoptysis (Hüesten vnd außwurff), and plague/poisoned wounds.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0009.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0009.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 4977 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0009.JP2#xywh=214,287,4542,6157 | Center Rule X=2501
Summary:      Page 32 (recto, numbered '32' in upper-right margin; faces p. 30 on verso Canvas 8, skipping '31' in pagination without text loss). Column A completes the recipe from p. 30, then gives an important historical note on Balsam of Copaiba ('Balsamo Copauia') recently imported from the Indies ('auß India') and used for remarkable cures in Vienna ('in Wienn' — confirming the manuscript's Austrian provenance), followed by surgical management of carious jawbone (incision, actual cautery, oil of vitriol, exfoliation) and syringe-injections for dental fistulae. Column B features a half-column watercolour bust portrait of a mustachioed gentleman in a red doublet and wide pleated ruff, above remedies for putrefaction/ulceration of the mouth ('Von fälung des Mundts', stomatitis/scurvy), including a pauper's remedy ('arme leüd die nichts Vermögen') of watercress, scurvy-grass, and horseradish.
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p32_gentleman] #xywh=2501,287,2255,2993 : Watercolour Bust Portrait of a Gentleman in Red Doublet and Pleated Ruff (p. 32, Col. B Upper)

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0010.JP2#xywh=528,368,4553,6163 | Center Rule X=2785
Summary:      Page 33 (verso, numbered '33' in upper-left margin). Column A treats scraping necrotic gum roots with a razor ('schar mäser'), incarnative powders to make rotted gums grow back, tightening loose teeth ('Zant wagel'), a potent sublimate-and-alum water applied with a small screw/swab, and remedies for halitosis. Column B treats inflammation and swelling of the tonsils and uvula ('Mandl vnd Zäpffel'), including lead acetate ('bleÿ Zukher') gargles and the folk-surgical maneuver of pulling the patient hard by the earlobes to raise a fallen uvula ('Wan das Zäpffel abgefallen ziehe ihm Woll beÿ den ohr läpel'), followed by a watercolour drawing of four multi-rooted human molar teeth and the opening of the treatise on toothache ('Von den Zänten Zuestänten vnd khrankheiten').
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p33_teeth] #xywh=2850,3720,2200,930 : Watercolour Study of Four Extracted Human Molar Teeth (p. 33, Col. B Middle)

Summary:      Page 34 (recto, numbered '34' in upper-right margin). Continues the treatise on toothache ('Von Zant schmerzen') from p. 33. Distinguishes hot vs. cold catarrhal fluxions, observes that extraction ('herauß reiß') is the only permanent cure for carious teeth, and provides anodyne cotton-wool pellets, aural instillation of castoreum or horseradish juice, temporal plasters (Gum Elemi, mastic, opium), Laudanum opiatum, camphor ('XXX'), guaiacum-wine solar digests, and astrological/solar remedies using ash-wood ('lign. fraxino') gathered on St. John's Day (Midsummer) before sunrise ('Vor auf gang der ☉') and sorrel gathered in June before sunrise.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0012.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0012.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5417 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0012.JP2#xywh=211,243,4978,6312 | Center Rule X=2819
Summary:      Page 35 (verso, numbered '35' in upper-left margin). Column A covers remedies for carious teeth, non-surgical chemical shedding of rotten teeth ('Das die Zant auß falen') using mulberry root steeped in strong vinegar, tooth-preserving and whitening powders (burnt hartshorn, mastic, calcined salt), and infant teething remedies ('Das den khindern die Zant Paldt Wachsen') using butter, honey, and hare's brain ('hasen hirn') rubbed on the gums ('Zant Piller'). Column B opens with a watercolour illustration of a spotted frog ('Fröschel')—a visual pun on sublingual ranula ('Von Fröschel vnder der Zungen / ranula', literally 'little frog')—followed by medical and surgical treatment of ranula (astringent gargles, lancet incision, or venesection of the sublingual vein).
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p35_frog] #xywh=2819,243,2370,1787 : Watercolour Illustration of a Spotted Frog ('Fröschel' / Ranula Visual Mnemonic, p. 35, Col. B Upper)

Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0013.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5047 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0013.JP2#xywh=257,282,4567,6197 | Center Rule X=2543
Summary:      Page 36 (recto, numbered '36' in upper-right margin). Upper Column A displays a watercolour study of four human teeth (single-, two-, and three-rooted) above a candid first-person clinical warning on treating loose teeth ('Rogle Zant föst machen'): 'one reaps more disgrace than honor therewith... if it does not help you, do not blame me, blame your own sour scorbutic blood!'. Includes astringent electuaries, Croll's Lapis medicamentosus with Gum Lac, and live crayfish pounded with burdock root to regenerate gums. Column B treats tooth whitening and features a watercolour profile portrait of a patient injecting his mouth with a brass syringe, introducing 'Vnderschidtliche Mundt oder Einspritz Wasser' (mouth- and syringe-waters for loose teeth and mercurial salivation).
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p36_teeth] #xywh=257,282,2286,1168 : Watercolour Study of Four Single- and Multi-Rooted Human Teeth (p. 36, Col. A Upper)
  * [fig_p36_syringe] #xywh=2543,3780,2281,1620 : Watercolour Profile Portrait of a Patient Using a Brass Oral Syringe (p. 36, Col. B Middle)

Summary:      Page 37 (verso, numbered '37' in upper-left margin). Column A completes the syringe-injection water from p. 36, then gives a comprehensive Tormentil-root gargle for scurvy ('Mund fäul Scharbokh'), a honey-electuary for eroded gums, and a compound herbal mixture to be kept dried in a box ('in einer geschachtl behalten') for instant preparation of gargle-waters. Column B gives insufflation and gargle remedies for a prolapsed uvula (blowing celandine root powder, nitre '🜕', or sugar of lead 'Sachari ♄'), tonsillar abscesses, deep throat ulcers ('dieffe löcher im hals'), and mercurial salivation using oak bark and Album Graecum.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Summary:      Page 39 (fol. 20r) continues the treatise on Angina, distinguishing true 'Angina exquisita' (with high fever, thirst, and mortal danger of suffocation) from 'Angina spuria' (false angina). It provides prognostic signs ('NB: Pronostico') and outlines the urgent therapeutic regimen ('Die Chur'), emphasizing immediate clysters, repeated bloodletting (median vein, leeches, sublingual veins), and warm foot/arm baths.

Summary:      Page 40 (fol. 20v) continues the treatment of Angina with gentle cassia and tamarind laxatives, cooling initial gargle waters (with nightshade, rose water, and vinegar), resolving and ripening poultices/plasters (using marshmallow root, figs, swallow's nest, and lily root), and gargle waters and cupping glasses ('Ventosen') to break the aposteme and relieve severe throat pain and dyspnea.

Summary:      Page 48 (recto, numbered '48' in upper-right margin; opening anatomical plate of the Ophthalmology treatise). Features watercolour diagrams of the extraocular muscles, isolated ocular humors, and a multi-layered physical paper flap dissection ('fugitive sheet' / anatomical volvelle) of the human eye in Column A (whose lifted states are photographed on Canvases 727–730), paired with an anatomical treatise in Column B explaining labels A–R and the origin of the seven tunics from the cerebral meninges.
Laminated Flap States (Multi-Canvas IIIF Composite):
  * State 1 (Canvas #25, b18775275_MS_990_0025.JP2): #xywh=910,1520,1450,2270 — State 1 (Flaps Closed): Outer Tunic F (Conjunctiva/Sclera with vascular arborization), Cornea G, Pupil H, Optic Stalk A/B/D/E.
  * State 2 (Canvas #728, b18775275_MS_990_0728.JP2): #xywh=850,1520,1400,2270 — State 2 (First Flap F Lifted): Reveals Optic Nerve Sheath K-K, Dark Choroid/Uvea Tunic I (with vascular arborization), and Pupil/Iris H/R.
  * State 3 (Canvas #729, b18775275_MS_990_0729.JP2): #xywh=850,1350,1400,2440 — State 3 (Second Flap I Lifted): Reveals Net-like Retina Tunic L (Tunica retiformis ò retina) enclosing the Vitreous Humor.
  * State 4 (Canvas #730, b18775275_MS_990_0730.JP2): #xywh=850,1350,1400,2440 — State 4 (Third Flap L Lifted — Deepest Interior): Reveals Optic Nerve Core m, Vitreous Humor n, Crystalline Lens o, and Aqueous Humor P.
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p48_muscles_lat] #xywh=250,280,1270,1280 : Diagram A: Eye in its form with extraocular muscles elevated
  * [fig_p48_muscles_post] #xywh=1220,250,1320,1830 : Diagram A–I, a: Posterior/frontal stellate view of the six extraocular muscles, trochlea G, sclera H, optic nerve I, and motor nerve twigs a
  * [fig_p48_lens_aranea] #xywh=450,1820,460,410 : Diagram B: Crystalline humor with the tunica aranea
  * [fig_p48_lens_bare] #xywh=520,2470,270,270 : Diagram D: Crystalline humor bare and alone
  * [fig_p48_vitreus] #xywh=1950,2120,420,320 : Diagram C: Posterior white vitreous humor with the crystalline lens
  * [fig_p48_flap_eye] #xywh=910,1520,1450,2270 : Laminated Multi-Layer Flap Dissection of the Eye (Labels A–R across 4 physical states, Canvases 25 & 727–730)

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0026.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0026.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5532 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0026.JP2#xywh=688,274,4643,6271
Summary:      Page 49 (verso, numbered '49' in upper-left margin; full-width single-column layout across the red-ruled frame, cited in Wellcome catalogue 'Pp. 49-165 are devoted to ophthalmology'). Completes the sentence from p. 48 col. B l. 53 ('genand Cornea'), then treats: (1) The Three Humors of the Eye (Vitreus, Crystallinus, Albugineus/Aquosus, noting that cataract arises in the anterior aqueous humor); (2) The Six Extraocular Muscles (noting the Vesalian observation that the 7th retractor bulbi muscle exists only in beasts/cattle and not in humans); and (3) A scholastic Latin-German synthesis of the parts, nerves, vessels, glands, and tunics constituting the eye.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Summary:      Page 50 (recto, numbered '50' in upper-right margin; continuing the Ophthalmology Treatise from p. 49). Column A completes the description of the Cornea/Sclera, describes the Uvea/Choroid (originating from the pia mater), the Pupil and ciliary interstice, and cites Jean Riolan (Anthropographia lib. 4, cap. 6) on why only two universal tunics (Cornea and Uvea) truly merit the name Tunica. Column B describes the Aranea (capsule), Retina, and Vitreous tunic, then opens the section 'Von den humoribus der Augen Vnd wie das gesicht gemacht wirdt' (Of the Humors of the Eyes and How Vision is Produced), detailing the aqueous and crystalline humors. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 51 (verso, numbered '51' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the anatomical physiology of the crystalline and vitreous humors and explains the Galenic-Renaissance theory of vision ('Visio das gesicht') as the meeting of external visible species with internal visual spirits flowing down the optic nerve. Column B opens the clinical ophthalmology section with a bold red rubric ('Hier fang ich an, in Namen Gottes Von den khrankheiten der augen, Jnerlich vnd Eüserlich'), citing Pliny the Elder's attribution of 365 diseases to the eye alone and framing blindness with the proverb 'Ain Blinder Man — ain armer Man'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Column A features a large half-column watercolour portrait of a young man in a crimson gold-trimmed cap exhibiting bilateral pale/cloudy cataract pupils, above a red-rubric classification of the four principal causes of eye disease ('Die khrankheiten der augen bestehen in 4 Vrsachen'). Column B opens the clinical treatise on cataracts ('Erstens Was der Staan oder Cataracta ist / Seÿ' and 'Wie die Cataracta Erwachssen vnd in die augen khumen'), describing the five colors of cataract (white, gray, yellow, green, blue), noting that white and gray cataracts are the most common and easiest to couch/cure by an experienced oculist ('Erfahrnen Oculisten'). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 53 (verso, numbered '53' in upper-left margin). Column A enumerates six internal and external causes of cataracts (brain, phlegmatic blood, foul stomach/spleen/liver vapors, coarse foods like onions, garlic, horseradish, mustard, smoked meat, peas, and lentils, excessive weeping, and trauma), and refutes the common belief that a cataract must take 7 years to ripen, citing the author's own clinical experience curing patients blind for only 6 months to 2 years. Column B lists the prodromal signs of cataract ('Von den Zaichen des Staan': cobwebs, floaters/flies, nets, fog, colored halos, diplopia, congenital cataract) and explains how to distinguish gastric vs. cranial origin ('die Vrsach Zuerkhenen ob sÿe Seÿ auß dem Magen oder haubt') by fluctuation with meals, time of day, lunar phase, and weather. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 55 (verso, numbered '55' in upper-left margin). Column A gives a steam-fumigation ('Ain Guette Bähung Vor den Weißen Starn') using eyebright, white lily, valerian, fennel, and basil, paired with a half-column watercolour illustration ('Figur Wie Man sich Zum Bähen Schikhen soll') depicting a patient in a green coat with red cuffs holding a steaming pot under a white linen cloth tent. Column B records sympathetic/amuletic wearing of Verbena (for white/green cataracts in men, yellow for women) and blue chicory root dug on St. John's Day in the waning moon, then opens 'Von den Grauen Star' (Of the Gray Cataract) and its preventive powder and fumigation. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p55_ocular_steaming] #xywh=400,3180,2250,3300 : Figur: Patient Performing Ocular Steam Fumigation (p. 55, Col. A Lower)

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0033.JP2

Summary:      Page 60 (recto, numbered '60' in upper-right margin; pagination jumps from 55 to 60 without textual loss). Column A completes the steaming recipe from p. 55, displays Portrait No. 2 ('Figur des Grauben Staan', showing gray-ash cataract pupils), and adds a second steaming recipe ('Ein Andere Bähung Vor den grauen Starn') and the start of an eye-water. Column B completes the green copper/sal-ammoniac eye-water with an inlaid watercolour diagram of wick-filtration/decanting through a red felt strip ('filzl rodes düch') into a glass flask, followed by an alembic-distilled eye-water and an electuary ('Volgente Lattwerung Ist Sehr khöstlich') to strengthen the eyes and clear the optic nerves. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0034.JP2#xywh=360,200,4760,6300 | Center Rule X=2680
Summary:      Page 61 (verso, numbered '61' in upper-left margin). Column A prescribes an early regimen to prevent cataracts ('den Starn Züeverhindern') combining cranial purgations (Extractum Catholicum, diagrydium pills), venesection, tea/decoction ('Thee vnd Chaus' = tea and coffee/cacao?), and vitrum antimonii/camphor collyria. Column B finishes a collyrium, presents a famous eye-water credited with curing a man blind for 9 years ('Volgentes Wasser hat ainen geholffen der 9 Jahr blindt war'), and opens the clinical manual on examining cataract patients ('Volgt Wie Man Guett vnd bösse Menge der augen Underschiden Soll')—instructing the oculist to interrogate the patient carefully before couching. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0035.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5095 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0035.JP2#xywh=180,180,4620,6340 | Center Rule X=2520
Summary:      Page 62 (recto, numbered '62' in upper-right margin). Column A details the hands-on clinical examination before cataract couching: pressing the thumb onto the upper eyelid over the pupil and releasing quickly to check pupillary dilation/contraction and cataract mobility, inspecting obliquely for white adhesive threads (synechiae) binding the cataract to the cornea or uvea, and condemning unscrupulous practitioners who apply corrosive 'atz' (vitriol, alum, green stone, burnt stone) that ruin the cornea. Column B finishes that condemnation, presents Portrait No. 5 ('Figur des bösen Mangel der augen', showing constricted/irregular pupils), and opens 'Es ist auch ein andere ardt des Starn' describing congenital/innate constricted pupils. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 63 (verso, numbered '63' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the discussion of painful/constricted cataracts with Portrait No. 6 ('Die andre figur, der bössen augen'), depicting a woman in a striped veil and yellow pleated collar. Column B opens the treatise on Black Cataract / Amaurosis ('Von dem Schwartzen Starn oder Gutta Serena Genandt'), stating that once the visual spirits are extinguished there is no hope, and enumerating six causes: optic-nerve obstruction, head trauma, severe headache, fever, pestilence, and pregnancy-induced blindness where women go blind during gestation and recover after delivery. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 64 (recto, numbered '64' in upper-right margin). Column A displays Portrait No. 4 ('Figur des Schwartzen Starn oder Gutta Serena') showing a woman in a striped green-and-yellow wimple with widely dilated, staring pupils, followed by 'Wie Man Erkhenen Soll ain vnd andere Vrsach' (distinguishing optic-nerve obstruction from intraocular corruption). Column B distinguishes two kinds of black cataract—including 'der frauen starn' (gestational amaurosis lasting 3–6 months until childbirth)—and discusses prognosis ('Wie Züerkhenen ob auf ain hilff Zü hoffen seÿ oder nit') and 'Von der khur des Schwartzen Starn'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 65 (verso, numbered '65' in upper-left margin). Column A displays Portrait No. 3 ('Figur der andern ardt des Schwartzen Starn'), depicting a mustachioed gentleman in a dark high-collared doublet with wide dark pupils, followed by purgative rhubarb-diagrydium pills, vesicatoria, and 'Ain guette Haubt Waschung Zue den Schwartzen starn'. Column B completes the head-wash, prescribes a sarsaparilla syrup ('Syrup in disen Züestandt'), an electuary powder with ambergris and musk, a soothing salve ('Ain Guettes Sälbel Wan die Vrsach in hiren vnd Neruen Jst'), and opens 'Von dem Schwartzen Star, So sein Vrsach Von Verfaulter Verdorbner feüghtigkhait Jst'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 66 (recto, numbered '66' in upper-right margin). Column A covers bloodletting and vesicatoria for younger patients, an electuary ('Lattwerung Vor den Schwartzen Starn'), a sternutatory snuff ('Volgentes Nies Pulluer Jst auch gar guett'), a row of five painted apothecary jars and square glass bottles, and the opening of 'Alda Will Jch dier offenbahren khöstliche Recept, welliche in anfangenten Schwartzen Starn Zü brauchen seindt'. Column B prescribes a strict diet excluding onions, garlic, horseradish, salted/smoked meat, geese, and ducks, warns against midday naps and excess drinking, and gives 'Haubt Pillulen' with temporal bloodletting. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 67 (verso, numbered '67' in upper-left margin). Column A finishes a distilled eye-water, presents two 'Augen stärkhentes diet' eye-strengthening powders, 'Ein khöstliches Wasser Zü stärkhung der augen', and 'Ain Anders' (boiling celandine flowers and leaves in rainwater). Column B finishes an electuary, presents 'Ain Wein das Gesicht Zü stärkhen' (medicated wine laid in a small cask until January) and a second eye-wine ('Ain anders'), and 'Lattwerung das gesicht Zu stärkhen'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 68 (recto, numbered '68' in upper-right margin). Opens the surgical manual for cataract couching ('Wie Man die Cataracta khinstlich abnemen Soll. Sufusian. Cataracta oder Staan'). Column A specifies the optimal seasons (spring or autumn, never hot summer or cold winter), waning moon ('☾'), exact dimensions and materials of the couching needle (5 finger-breadths total: 3 handle, 2 needle; gold, silver, or steel, smooth and polished), and the three best zodiacal signs (Libra, Virgo, Scorpio). Column B covers pre-operative interrogation (headache, fever, epilepsy, pregnancy), purgation 2–3 days prior, fasting on the day of operation, clearing the air/weather, and choosing a bright room with a seat for the patient. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0042.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0042.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5547 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0042.JP2#xywh=360,200,4760,6300 | Center Rule X=2680
Summary:      Page 69 (verso, numbered '69' in upper-left margin). Provides the complete step-by-step operative manual for cataract couching ('Sufusian'). Column A describes positioning the patient facing a window on a stool, the oculist facing him with the patient's hands resting on the oculist's knees, an assistant holding the head against his chest, bandaging the sound eye, using the right hand for the left eye and left hand for the right eye, parting the eyelids, and inserting the needle 1.5 knife-backs from the cornea through the conjunctiva. Column B details passing behind the uvea without touching the crystalline lens, depressing the cataract into the lower vitreous, holding it down for 2 or 3 Paternosters ('2 od[er] 3 Vatter Vnser'), withdrawing the needle, and managing a rising or tough/adherent cataract. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 70 (recto, numbered '70' in upper-right corner). Full-page watercolour operative scene labeled '#.o 7.' depicting three Franciscan friars in brown cowled habits with knotted rope girdles inside an infirmary chamber with a tiled floor, leaded-glass four-pane window, and iron-hinged door. One friar stands behind holding the seated friar-patient's head against his chest, while the friar-oculist sits facing him and couches a cataract in the patient's right eye with a steel needle; a yellow surgical table beside them holds two spare couching needles, two folded square compresses, a blue ceramic bowl (for egg-white/rose-water), and a curved linen bandage. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0044.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5517 x 6853 px)

Summary:      Page 71 (verso, numbered '71' in upper-left margin). Column A completes the operative technique for tearing/dissolving stubbornly rising cataracts and managing synechial adhesions to the uvea or cornea, followed by Portrait '#8.' ('Figur Wie man das Jnstrument in das aug sezt') showing a woman with a couching needle inserted horizontally into the temporal sclera of her right eye. Column B presents Figure '#.o 9.' ('Wie die Jnstrumendt oder Star Nadl Sein Sollen') illustrating three detailed couching needles (one plain, two spiral-fluted with pommels), rejects gold and silver needles in favor of tempered steel because a tough conjunctiva bends soft metals, and opens 'Wie Sich der Patient in der khur Verhalten Soll' (post-operative bed rest and fasting for 2 hours before broth). Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

PAGE / FOLIO: 72 (recto) | IIIF Canvas #45 (b18775275_MS_990_0045.JP2)
Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0045.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0045.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5366 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0045.JP2#xywh=180,180,4780,6340 | Center Rule X=2600
Summary:      Page 72 (recto, numbered '72' in upper-right margin). Column A details post-operative care: keeping the head elevated, fasting 2 hours before broth, drinking barley-water with fennel/anise, eating only soft spoon-foods (broths, poached eggs, almond milk, strained barley—nothing requiring chewing), avoiding coughing, sneezing, or loud noise, keeping the room quiet, changing bandages 3–4 times daily, and carefully turning the patient in bed after half an hour. Column B lists the six contraindications to couching ('Welliche Augen durch das Jnstrument gefährlich Zü khurieren': epilepsy, fever/headache, small deep-set eyes, squinting/nystagmus, pregnancy, and menstruation/amenorrhea), then opens 'Von der khur des Weisen Starn' and 'Das Erste Pandt Zum Weisen Starn' (first bandage using 6 egg-whites beaten with chicory water and flax/tow pledgets). Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 74 (recto, numbered '74' in upper-right corner—partially trimmed/faint). Column A gives post-operative unbandaging instructions ('Volgt kheider Von Verbinden des Starn'): keeping the eyes bound 2–3 days, sitting up on day 3–4, gradual light exposure after 6–12 days depending on cataract maturity, and avoiding candle/firelight for 3–4 weeks. Column B features Portrait #12 showing a man wearing a green/blue taffeta eye-shade visor ('ein düchel Vor den augen hangeth, so Von grüen oder blau Taffet ist'), then opens 'Von den Zuefällen Welliche Sich Bisweillen in diser khur begeben' (Post-Operative Complications), beginning with Complication 1: 'Erster Zuefall. Wo der Starn angewachsen'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Covers Complication 1 bandage ('Das Erste Pandt Züe dem angewachsenen starn' with tormentil water and camphor), Complication 2 ('der 2. Zuefall Wan ain aug mit dem Jnstrument Verlezet worden': injury to the retina/aranea or intraocular bleeding, with two collyria using rue seed, camphor, betony, white lily, dragon's blood, and rose water), and Complication 3 ('der 3. Zuefall Jst Grosse Hiz vnd Rötte': post-operative heat and redness, with cooling waters of houseleek/sempervivum, nightshade, terra sigillata, spermaceti, camphor, and raw egg-white with vinegar). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0049.JP2#xywh=180,180,4700,6340 | Center Rule X=2580
Summary:      Page 78 (recto, numbered '78' in upper-right margin; pagination jumps from 75 to 78 without textual loss). Column A opens Complication 4 ('der 4 Zuefall. Wan grosse Schmerzen in die augen khumen') and analyzes three causes of severe post-operative pain ('Woher Soliche Schmerzen khumen'): (1) inexperienced oculists using thick, unpolished needles that let the vitreous humor escape; (2) improper piercing and overly tight bandaging; (3) cold drafts entering the eye before healing. Column B adds emotional/environmental triggers (anger, fright, weeping, wind, smoke, sleeplessness, hard stools) and prescribes 'Mitel Vor grosse Reisen vnd Wehe tag des haubts' (senna-tamarind purge) and 'Ein anders Purgier Tränckhel' followed by cephalic venesection and vesicatoria behind the ears. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Column A gives four pain-relief remedies: 'Ain Guette haubt Waschung Vor den grosen Schmerzen des haubts', 'Ain guettes Triet Puluer Vor die Haubt Schmerzen', 'Ain anders Guettes Tranckh', 'Ain Guettes Sälbel Vor den Schmerzen' (containing dissolved Laudanum to anoint the temples and forehead), and 'Auf die Augen Zü legen' (poppy, henbane, lead, camphor, wine, and rose water). Column B opens Complication 5 ('der finffte Zuefall. Wan die augen Sehr mit Wasser fließen': excessive tearing / epiphora after couching), prescribing Cassia purgation, vesicatoria, astringent powder, and 'Ain guettes Wasser Vor das wäsern der augen'. Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0051.JP2

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0051.JP2#xywh=180,180,4680,6340 | Center Rule X=2580
Summary:      Page 80 (recto, numbered '80' in upper-right margin). Column A finishes the eye-water, presents 'Ain Anders guettes Wasser' (using red tormentil, white lily, tutia, camphor, and rainwater), Complication 6 ('der Sechste Zuefall. Wan die augen nach dem khur das Liecht nit Leiden khünen': post-operative photophobia), and opens Complication 7 ('der Sibende Zuefall Schwindl des haubts': vertigo). Column B gives 'Ain guettes Puluer Vor den Schwindl' (burnet-saxifrage, fennel, anise, cubebs, galangal), then treats Complication 8 ('der achte Zuefall. Wan Vor den augen alles Scheinet rodt, grüen, gelb, blau, weiss': post-operative chromatopsia and floaters—distinguishing leftover cataract matter in the aqueous humor from blood in the conjunctiva or fragmented particles), prescribing cassia purgation and venesection. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 81 (verso, numbered '81' in upper-left margin). Column A gives 'Ain Guettes Wasser Zue gemelten mangel' (blue chicory, blue cornflower/rittersporn, white lily), then treats Complication 9 ('der Neünte Zuefall. Jst grosse geschwulst des augs. vnd der Coniunctiua': chemosis/conjunctival swelling, with a plaster of white incense, myrrh, camphor, alum, and egg-white, plus pomegranate-peel water and fenugreek/sarcocolla collyrium). Column B treats Complication 10 ('der Zehente Zuefall. Wan ain gestochener starn aufstehet. vnd Sich Widerumb Vor legt': re-ascent of a couched cataract), noting that if the cataract was properly loosened and not torn, it often dissolves and clears spontaneously over time—citing cases of patients blind for half or a whole year who spontaneously regained their sight! Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0053.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0053.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5282 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0053.JP2#xywh=180,180,4700,6340 | Center Rule X=2580
Summary:      Page 82 (recto, numbered '82' in upper-right margin). Column A prescribes purgation, vesicatoria, 'Ain guette Lattwerung Züe den aufgestignen Starn', and 'Ain guettes Wasser Zü disen Zuefall', then opens the major treatise on Lacrimal Fistula ('Von den fistlen der augen — fistula Lacrimale'), describing how smallpox or salty humors ulcerate the inner canthus and erode the lacrimal bone (os lacrimale / caries). Column B warns that chirurgians who fail to treat lacrimal fistulae carefully risk great harm, explains how pressing a finger at the inner canthus beside the nose expresses white/purulent matter ('weisse vnd häutige materj'), and displays a half-column watercolour portrait of a nun in a black veil and white wimple pressing her finger to a weeping, blood-streaked lacrimal fistula in her right inner canthus, concluding that the surest cure is incision and actual cautery. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0054.JP2#xywh=360,200,4760,6300 | Center Rule X=None
Summary:      Page 83 (verso, numbered '83' in upper-left corner). Full-width layout flanking a large central watercolour operative scene labeled '#.o 1.' showing a nun seated in a wooden chair with her wrists tied with red ribbons to the armrests, blood streaming from her incised right lacrimal fistula, supported by two nuns behind her (one holding a crucifix) while a third nun watches through the doorway and a bearded Franciscan friar-oculist approaches holding a lancet and white linen cloth beside a surgical table bearing flasks, red jars, and knives. The upper text specifies pre-operative preparation (purgation, venesection, plaster, and tying the patient's hands to the chair); the lower text instructs the assistant to steady the head and guides the surgeon in incising down to the bone without cutting the tear-sac or lower eyelid. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 84 (recto, numbered '84' in upper-right corner). Column A features Portrait '#.2' of a nun with blood flowing from her incised right lacrimal fistula, explaining how to incise down to the bone with a lancet, pack the wound with a dry sponge tent until the next day, apply a digestive ointment for 3–4 days, and insert small sponge tents. Column B illustrates three surgical knives/lancets ('#.o 3.': curved bistoury, folding lancet in decorated sheath, and straight scalpel), then details cauterizing the carious bone with a hooked actual cautery iron ('#.o 4.') while shielding the eyeball with a curved metal eye-shield ('#.o 4.' at bottom). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 85 (verso, numbered '85' in upper-left margin). Column A illustrates three curved/spherical actual cautery irons ('#.o 5.') with turned wooden handles for cauterizing the lacrimal bone, followed by post-cautery digestive salve, 'Ain khöstliches Wasser Zü haillen den schon gebrandten augen fistl', 'Ain andere Reinigung' (honey, nihil album, aloes, aristolochia), and 'Volgents Sälbel brauch Zur Haillung'. Column B gives a healing salve (myrrh, sarcocolla, frankincense, aloes, mastic, dragon's blood), 'Ain Herliches Pflaster auf die fistel Zum Verbinden', and opens 'Widerumb ain andere Weiß dise fistel Zü Churieren' using a caustic escharotic ('Ain herliche Ezung in die augen fistel') instead of hot iron. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 86 (recto, numbered '86' in upper-right margin). Column A gives 'Ain andere ezung. Züe den augen fistlen' (quicklime, orpiment, white alum boiled in vinegar), 'Ain herliches Wasser Züe den augen in ezen vnd brenen', 'Ain guets deffensiff Zü beschüzung der augen', purgation notes, and 'NB: Volgentes Solle der arzt woll mörckhen' (distinguishing fistula from brain vs. blood). Column B advises on venesection and gives three internal fistula potions ('Volgentes Tranckh Jst Sehr khöstlich in den augen fistlen', 'Ain anders Tranckh, Wan die Vrsach Von geblüedt Jst', 'Ain anders Tranckh Zü beiderleÿ augen fistel') plus 'Ain guets Waser in die fistl'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0058.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0058.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5484 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0058.JP2#xywh=360,200,4760,6300 | Center Rule X=2680
Summary:      Page 87 (verso, numbered '87' in upper-left margin). Opens the alternative surgical method for lacrimal fistula: trephining/perforating the lacrimal bone ('Es ist noch ein andere Weiß vnd manier die augen fistel Zü Churieren. Namblich durch das perforieren oder durch born'). Column A details pre-operative accumulation of pus for 3–4 days, bandaging the sound eye, incising down to the bone, and widening with sponge tents. Column B describes perforating the 'os cribrum' (ethmoid/lacrimal bone) with the spiral-tipped bone drill shown in Figure '#.o 6.' ('Form vnd gestalt der Jnstrument Zum durch born'), illustrating three slender metal drills with auger tips and turned wooden handles. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p87_bone_drills] #xywh=3560,3560,1520,2900 : Instrument Plate #6: Three Spiral Bone Drills / Perforators (p. 87, Col. B Lower)

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0059.JP2#xywh=180,180,4760,6340 | Center Rule X=None
Summary:      Page 88 (recto, numbered '88' in upper-right corner). Features a large upper watercolour operative scene showing the Franciscan friar-surgeon standing at the surgical table on the left while two nuns attend the nun-patient seated in a red-cushioned armchair (her wrists bound with white cloths, blood at her right inner canthus) and a fourth nun enters the doorway holding a yellow medicine flask. Below, full-width text completes the trephining post-op dressing ('mit praecipitat. oder ainen andern ezing Pulluer') and explains ('damit du aber wissest was das durch bohren Nüze') how boring an opening into the nasal cavity redirects lacrimal fluid downward into the throat and nose rather than weeping over the eye. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 89 (verso, numbered '89' in upper-left margin). Opens the treatise on external ocular films and scars ('Von Allerleÿ Eüsserlichen fell vnd Maill Welliche über die augen Waxssen das gesicht Ver hindern vnd Verderben'), beginning with smallpox corneal/conjunctival pannus ('Erstlich Von den Bladter fellen der augen', 'ungula ex pustulis') and a digesting decoction of wild chicory, vervain, eyebright, mallow, rhubarb, and fennel. Column B features Portrait '.A.' (mustachioed man in red cap with lateral corneal opacity) and Portrait '.B.' (mustachioed man with bilateral pale corneal films) flanking a short purgation note. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Column A gives a blistering cantharides plaster ('Ain gar guettes Zengen Pflaster'), 'Ain guette Waichung Züe denen Bladter fellen' (marshmallow, rue, chamomile, melilot), and 'Ain Edles Wasser Vor die Bladter fell' (cornflower, frankincense, tragacanth, sarcocolla, pearls, camphor). Column B adds 'Ain Anders guets Wasser' and 'Ain Edles Pulluer Zue den Bladtern' (prepared sapphire, tutty, coral, pearls, camphor, white vitriol), then opens 'Von den Brandt fellen der augen' (corneal burns / panni ex ambustione from fire sparks, coals, or blows) with 'Ain guetts Bähung Zü den Brand fellen'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 91 (verso, numbered '91' in upper-left margin). Column A finishes the burn steaming, gives 'Ain guettes Wasser Vor die Brandt fell' (blue cornflower water, honey, burnt crab-shells, sal ammoniac, galbanum), 'Ain anders Sehr guettes Wasser' (blackberry water, white vitriol, alum), 'Ain gar güettes Pulluer Vor die Brandt fell' (vitriol, cuttlefish bone, sarcocolla, red coral, white vitriol), and 'Weider begeben Sich andere Abscheüe Zur Brandt der augen' (burn ulcers of the eyelids and globes). Column B completes the burn-blister salve (poppy oil, camphor, sparrow fat), gives 'Ain guetts Wasser Zü den Verbrenten augen', and opens 'Von andern außwendigen Weißen vnd grauben fellen'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0063.JP2#xywh=180,180,4740,6340 | Center Rule X=2580
Summary:      Page 92 (recto, numbered '92' in upper-right margin). Column A gives 'Ain guettes Pulluer für Bladter vnd Brandt fell' (white coral, prepared tutty, cuttlefish bone, pearls, sarcocolla, sugar candy, musk), illustrated with a watercolour row of three blue-and-white ceramic apothecary jars, followed by 'Ain Sehr Edles Sälbel für die Bladter vnd Brandt fell' (crocus metallorum, tutty, calamine, burnt vitriol), a bear-grease/viper-fat/butter salve ('Bälbel' / 'Ain Anders' / 'Ain anders gar guettes Sälbel'). Column B illustrates a hard-boiled egg ('Augen Wasser Von airn'), explaining how to cut a hot hard-boiled egg in half, remove the yolk, and fill the cavity with white vitriol/alum/camphor to collect therapeutic eye-drops in four variants. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 94 (recto, numbered '94' in upper-right margin). Column A finishes the wonderful eye-water (boil 12 hours, cured a man blind for 10 years in 40 days!), gives 'khöstliches augen Waser für fell vnd Maill', 'Ain anders gar khöstliches augen Waser' (sal ammoniac, alum, white vitriol, celandine, eyebright, cornflower, aged in a brass pot until sky-blue, then sun-distilled), and 'Ain Anders für die fell'. Column B lists powder/drop variants, 'Saffier Waser für Maill vnd fell' (limewater + sal ammoniac in a brass vessel turning sapphire-blue), and 'Das grüene augen Waser' (virgin honey, vitriol, sal ammoniac, white lead, aged in a brass vessel until green, then sun-distilled). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 96 (recto, numbered '96' in upper-right margin). Column A gives four remedies for watery films: 'Ain gar guettes Wasser für dise fell' (hematite, red coral, ivory, rose-water), 'Ain anders Wasser' (coral, tutty, sugar candy in Malmsey), 'Ain ander khöstliches Wasser' (mallow, elderflower, tormentil, alum, vitriol), 'Ain anders guettes Wasser' (larkspur, chicory, cornflower, camphor), and 'Ain guets Pulluer für die Waser fell'. Column B gives an NB warning against irritating inflamed eyes with sharp waters (offering a cooling strawberry/endive/camphor/alum collyrium), then opens 'Von den Blüett vnd fleisch fellen der augen' (pterygium / Sebel / panniculus carnosus), requiring rapid surgical treatment and bloodletting. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Column A prescribes 'Ain guets Waser für die fleisch fell' (celandine, burnt alum, verdigris), 'Ain anders Edles Pulluer' (hematite, burnt ivory, myrrh, long pepper, white vitriol), 'Ain anders Pulluer', and then opens the surgical excision of advanced pterygium (seating the patient in a low armchair bound by hands and feet). Column B displays a watercolour figure of a mustachioed man in a white doublet and green breeches seated in a red-backed wooden armchair ready for pterygium surgery, and below details passing a curved needle with a silk thread ('seiden faden') under the fleshy film to lift and excise it cleanly without piercing the cornea or conjunctiva. Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 98 (recto, numbered '98' in upper-right margin). Column A displays Portrait '.D.' ('Figur der fleisch fell') showing a mustachioed man in a gold-trimmed tunic with intensely red vascular pterygia encroaching across both eyes, followed by surgical completion: lifting the silk thread in the left hand and excising the pterygium with a sharp knife without cutting the thread or injuring the globe, plus a styptic collyrium. Column B gives a healing egg-white/terra-sigillata plaster and 'Augen Wasser Zue den abgenomen fleisch fellen', then opens 'Von den Mükhen oder fliegen maill der augen' (dark corneal spots/maculae resembling flies or gnats). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 99 (verso, numbered '99' in upper-left margin). Column A finishes describing fly-spot corneal maculae (which obscure vision like a cobweb or thread), displays Portrait '.E.' ('Figur der Mukh Maill': young woman with a green leaf hair ornament and red ribbon choker), and begins 'Ain guets Tranckh die scharffe feüghtigkhait Zü digeriern'. Column B finishes the digestive decoction and cassia purge, gives 'Ain khöstliches Waser für dise Maill', 'Ain anders Waser', 'Ain guettes Pulluer' (white frankincense, mastic, burnt crab-eyes, amber, camphor), and opens the major treatise on chronic hot and cold ocular fluxes ('Von den bösen vnd lang wehrenten augen flüsen. Rinen. hizigen vnd Rinnen der augen'). Transcribed with Gemini 4.

Summary:      Page 100 (recto, numbered '100' in upper-right margin). Column A displays Portrait '.F.' of a woman with fiercely bloodshot, weeping eyes and tear streaks down her cheeks, explaining below that chronic fluxes are of two kinds—hot and cold—and detailing hot fluxes eroding the eyeball and causing blindness. Column B prescribes 'Ain guettes Tranckh Zü den hizigen augen flüsen' (wild chicory, dodder, fumitory, rue, borage), Electuarium de succo rosarum, cupping/venesection, 'Ain guette Bähung in hizigen augen flüß', 'Ain guettes Waser für die haisen flüß in die augen', and 'Ain anders khöstliches Waser für die hizigen flüß'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 101 (verso, numbered '101' in upper-left margin). Column A gives 'Ain Guette Bähung', 'Ain guets augen Wasser', cooling compresses for hot eye fluxes, 'Waser für Entzintung vnd schmerzen der augen' (with opium and women's milk), and 'Ain anders' (baked/roasted apple poultice with butter, sugar, and saffron). Column B adds 'Ain anders für hiz vnd schmerzen' (adding 2–3 grains opium if pain is severe), 'Ain anders für grosse Schmerzen vnd flüß Von geblüedt', 'dises stelt den flus auf', 'Ain anders Wo Zü ruth seind', 'Ain anders so den flus Zurükh helt', an NB on purging and applying fennel/vervain/rose infusion, and opens 'für Grosse Schmerzen'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 102 (recto, numbered '102' in upper-right margin). Column A covers fenugreek mucilage, 'für Rotte augen' (camphor, tutty, aloes, white sugar, rose-water), 'Ain anders der gleichen', 'Ain anders für schmerzen vnd Rötte', 'Ain anders für flüßige rodte vnd rinnente augen' (fresh wormwood on flax pledget with egg-white), 'Sälbel für den hizigen fluß Wunder bahrlich' (fresh butter, camphor, tutty, sugar candy washed in vinegar), and 'Ain anders khöstliches Sälbel'. Column B completes a honey/camphor/butter salve, gives 'Defensiuo für flüßige augen', 'Ain anders für die flüß', 'für Schmerzen der augen', 'für Schmerzen vnd Frenen der augen', 'Ung. Neapoleum', guaiacum wood-drink ('lignum sanctum'), and 'für Endtzindung der augen lider'. Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 103 (verso, numbered '103' in upper-left margin). Column A finishes the white-bread/egg-yolk eyelid cataplasm, gives 'Ain anders' (mullein, bean flower, rue, violet, rose waters), 'Ain anders für Endtzintung schmerzen vnd fliessen', 'Ain anders', and 'Ain Wunderbahrliches Waser für Maill vnd flüß' (lime-water, egg-whites, sal ammoniac beaten in a brass vessel until green, illustrated by the brass vessels on Col. B). Column B displays a watercolour of three gleaming brass/gold basins on a shelf ('fig_p103_three_brass_vessels'), followed by 'Ain anders für augen hiz vnd Rötte' (sugar of lead, alum-egg) and an important clinical 'NB' warning oculists to distinguish cold fluxes (requiring warm steamings/baths) from hot salty fluxes (requiring cooling, bloodletting, and purging). Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 104 (recto, numbered '104' in upper-right margin). Column A prescribes 'In hizenden vnd hizigen flüßen ist diß Volgentes sehr herlich guett' (plantain, houseleek, rose, fennel, egg-white, camphor, white vitriol), 'Ain Anders' (steeping bruised rose-hip bark in egg-white), 'Ain Herliches Sälbel' (tutty, camphor, verdigris, washed butter), 'Volgents Sälbel Jst herlich vnd guett' (washed butter, sugar of lead, tutty, calamine, camphor), and 'Ain anders, Herliches Waser Vor die Enzintung der augen'. Column B completes the eye-water (tutty, camphor, red rose, burnet-saxifrage), adds a cooling egg-white/alum/saffron compress, presents 'Volgentes Jst ain Herliches Sälbl' (fresh butter, capon fat, white mercury precipitate, tutty), and opens 'für hizige geschwolne augen' (roasted/boiled apple pulp poultice). Transcribed with Gemini 4.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 105 (verso, numbered '105' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the poultice from p. 104 and opens 'Von khalten augen flüsen welche dise khumen. vnd wie sÿe Zü Churiern. .G.' above Portrait .G. (woman in blue headscarf weeping watery tears), explaining the three causes of cold ocular fluxes from brain moisture and head weakness, followed by 'Ein Herliches Trankh für khalte augen flüß'. Column B gives 'Ein Sehr Khöstliche Purgation in khalten augen flüsen', bloodletting and vesicatory advice, 'Ein guette haubt Salbung. für die khalte augen flüß', and 'Ein Edles Trankh für khalte flüß'.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p105_portrait_G] #xywh=380,1200,2280,2720 : Portrait .G.: Woman with Cold Weeping Eye Fluxes (p. 105, Col. A)

Column A gives five recipes for cold ocular fluxes: 'Ein Khöstliches wasser für die khalte flüß', 'Ein guettes Trankh. für den khalten flüß', 'Ein guettes augen wasser für die khalte flüß', 'Ein herliches Pülluer für die khalten flüß' (chewed in the mouth), and 'Ein guettes wasser darmit die augen auß Zü waschen'. Column B opens 'Von den alten lang wehr=enden bössen augen flüsen .H.' above Portrait .H. (dark-haired bearded man weeping dark tears), discussing chronic fluxes stemming from childhood smallpox, scurvy, syphilis, and long-standing head pains.

Summary:      Page 107 (verso, numbered '107' in upper-left margin). Column A introduces 'Wie man aber Solliche flüß begegen Soll. ist Volgents Zü Vernemben', recommending the neck seton ('Schnüer oder Setaceum oder Laqueum') above Figure .I. (large watercolour plate of the steel screw-clamp, needle, and red silk cord). Column B describes the full surgical technique: heating the needle tip red-hot, pinching up the skin of the nape with the clamp, piercing through the two holes, threading and knotting the buttered crimson silk cord, drawing it daily, and applying an escharotic salve if proud flesh threatens to close the wound.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 108 (recto, numbered '108' in upper-right margin). Column A displays Portrait .K. ('Figur wie die Schnüer in den hall Soll gelegt werden'), showing a weeping man in profile with the seton clamp attached to his nape and the red silk cord in place, followed by post-operative care with rose oil, diapalma plaster, digestive salve, and 'Ein herliches Sälbel Zur Schnüer Wan es mit fleisch will Züe=wachsen'. Column B adds Unguentum Apostolorum, Unguentum Aegyptiacum, 'Volgentes Sälbel Ist scharff vnd guett den flüß her wider Zü bring[en]', prognosis for desperate chronic fluxes, and opens the guaiacum wood-draught ('lignum sanctum') recipe.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 109 (verso, numbered '109' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the guaiacum wood-draught regimen (luting the pot, boiling, sweating for 2–3 hours for 6–8 weeks, biweekly purgation, monthly vesicatories, diet, and warning not to torment patients whose sight is already lost). Column B opens 'Von der lötzung der augen oder wan es ain aug gestochen wirdt' above Portrait .L. (woman in profile with blue hair ribbon and red coral necklace whose left eye is pierced by a knife), warning of deep wounds to the cornea, uvea, and loss of the crystalline humor.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p109_portrait_L] #xywh=2680,3560,2440,2900 : Portrait .L.: Woman with Penetrating Eye Injury (p. 109, Col. B)

Summary:      Page 110 (recto, numbered '110' in upper-right margin). Continues treatments for penetrating ocular wounds and loss of aqueous humor: greater celandine and calcined crayfish powder, camphorated celandine leaf extract with egg white, myrrh/bole in breastmilk, a cataplasm of eyebright/fennel/plantain, the prized 'elm-bladder sap' secret ('NB: dises mörke vnd gib dies groses archanum'), and an emergency salt-water dressing instructing the surgeon to bandage both eyes gently so the humor is not squeezed out.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 111 (verso, numbered '111' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the wound treatments from p. 110 (lukewarm red-wine bran poultice, beaten egg white, roasted egg-yolk/eyebright collyrium, green eye-shade over the healthy eye, warning against hot medicines in corneal vs. conjunctival wounds, and 'Ein Sehr guettes Pflaster Zü den Verlötzten augen'). Column B completes the tormentil healing water and opens 'Von abnemung des gesichts Blödigkheit dunkhle vnd Triebe der augen', discussing old age ('in old churches one finds dark windows'), phlegm-producing foods (garlic, peas, lentils, old cheese), and thick phlegm obstructing the optic nerve.
Model:        Gemini 4

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0083.JP2#xywh=300,180,4740,6280 | Center Rule X=2600
Summary:      Page 112 (recto, numbered '112' in upper-right margin). Column A discusses clouding of the vitreous and albugineous humors, weeping, looking at fire and snow, reading/writing small script at night, and excessive bloodletting, above Portrait .M. (bust wearing a yellow-orange patterned cap and dark-rimmed spectacles). Below Portrait .M., the text classifies eye colors (black as strongest, blue as weakest yet loveliest, grey as nimble) and eye sizes (small eyes sharper than large protruding eyes). Column B warns against delaying treatment ('Sight is the highest treasure, yet people often treat their eyes as if they had more eyes than fingers on their hand') and gives 'Ein khöstliches Pulver Zü stärkhen aines Schwachen gesicht' and 'Ein Arcana das gesicht Zü Stärkh[en]'.

Summary:      Page 113 (verso, numbered '113.' in upper-left margin). Column A gives age-graded ophthalmic arcana (40–50, 50–60, 60–70, 70–80, 80–100 years), including a small inline watercolour of a wooden drinking cup ('Tränkhlen. Von Eschig [holz]', ash-wood beaker) for restoring sight to the blind, plus golden/cochia pills for severe fluxes. Column B provides 'Ein khöstliches augen Wasser. Wan die augen schwach vnd Blödt sein weiche nicht mögen Zü schreiben oder Zü lesen', 'Augen Wasser Inerlich Zü stärkhen das schwache gesicht' (distilled in malmsey wine), and 'Ein khöstliches Pulver Zur stärkhung des gesichts' that restored a prelate's sight after ten years of blindness.
Model:        Gemini 4

Summary:      Page 114 (recto, numbered '114' in upper-right margin). Continues sight-strengthening recipes: 'Ein absonderliche Lattwerung Zü Stärkhung des gesichts' (eyebright/fennel/celandine electuary), 'Schwaches gesicht Zü stärkhen vnd Zü Conseruiern' (white onion juice & virgin honey, noting patients never needed spectacles again), 'Ein anders die augen Zü stärkhen' (honey boiled with an 8-year-old boy's urine), 'Die Conserua Von flor. Euphrasia', 'Zum Schwachen Gesicht', 'Zü stärkhung der Augen' (soft-roasted egg filled with vitriol), 'Das gesicht Zü stärkhen', and 'Ein herliches vnd khöstliches Wasser Zü stärkhen des gesicht' (malmsey wine, celandine, eyebright, quenched tutty, camphor, and aloes).
Model:        Gemini 4

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0086.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0086.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5521 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0086.JP2#xywh=360,180,4780,6320 | Center Rule X=2680
Summary:      Page 115 (verso, numbered '115.' in upper-left margin). Column A gives an eye-powder of rose sugar and cuttlefish bone, 'Beÿ Solchen augen Schwacheiten müsen auch Zü Zeiten guette haubt vnd augen Pillulen gebraucht werden' (Crato's amber pills with alhandal and diagridium), an herbal water blend, 'Augen stärkhentes Trisenet' (valerian/eyebright/cubeb spice powder), and 'Ein guetes Wasser Welliches das Gesicht hell vnd klar macht'. Column B treats obstructed optic nerves ('Wan die augen Neruen Verstopft brauch dises' with tormentil plaster and fennel eaten fasting), 'Von dunkhle augen', two distilled waters ('Ein guetes Wasser die augen Zü stärkh[en]'), and 'Ein Khöstliche Lattwerung' of fresh eyebright and fennel.
Model:        Gemini 4
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Summary:      Page 116 (recto, numbered '116' in upper-right margin). Column A gives a medicated wine bag ('Man khan auch Von augen drost Cimet vnd fenchel sam. ain säckhl machn'), eating 20 juniper berries every morning or sugar-coated Roman fennel seed, two spice powders ('Ein Khöstliches Pülluer für abnemb=ung des gesichts'), and 'Ein Säckhlein in Wein Zü henkhen für Schwacheit der augen'. Column B opens 'Dises ist ain Neues stükel Wie man das Verlohrne gesicht wider bring[en] khan' above Figure .N., a full-column watercolour showing a man in a yellow coat leaning over a table with a green bifurcated funnel over an earthenware pot directing celandine steam into both eyes.
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p116_portrait_N] #xywh=2620,1860,2400,3300 : Figure .N.: Patient Receiving Celandine Steam via Bifurcated Funnel (p. 116, Col. B)

Summary:      Page 117 (verso, numbered '117' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the celandine steam-funnel cure from p. 116 and displays Figure .O. ('Figur des Instruments'), a standalone watercolour of the green bifurcated funnel, followed by construction notes, 'Volgentes Wasser Soll man nach dem Bähen in die augen Than', and 'Augen stärkhente Latwerung'. Column B gives 'Gueiden Wein für ain schwaches gesicht', two eye-strengthening spirits ('Ein augen stärkhenten geist' and a hartshorn/saffron/castoreum spirit), 'Augen stärkhente Zeltel' (sugar lozenges with ambergris and musk), and 'Haubt vnd augen stärkhentes äpfel' (an aromatic pomander).
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p117_funnel_O] #xywh=380,1620,2280,1500 : Instrument Plate .O.: Bifurcated Eye-Steaming Funnel (p. 117, Col. A)

Summary:      Page 118 (recto, numbered '118' in upper-right margin). Column A gives 'Ein khöstliche Lattwerung Zü stärkhen der augen', 'Ein Schwacheit vnd Blödigkheit der augen' (volatile salts of hartshorn, amber, eyebright, mugwort, fennel, and rosemary; plus a spiced honey electuary held on the tongue so its vapors rise upward), and 'Volgentes haubt Pülluer Jst als ain schnüpff Tobakh Zü brauchen'. Column B adds valerian water in wine, 'augen stärkhente Zeltl', 'Schnüpff Puluer in Schwaheit der augn Zü brauchen', and opens the new chapter 'Von sachen aitern der augen' above Portrait .P. (youth with purulent discharge streaming from both eyes).
Model:        Gemini 4
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_p118_portrait_P] #xywh=2620,3440,2400,2540 : Portrait .P.: Youth with Purulent Eye Discharge (p. 118, Col. B)

Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0090.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0090.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5575 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0090.JP2#xywh=360,180,4780,6320 | Center Rule X=2680
Summary:      Page 119 (verso, numbered '119' in upper-left margin). Column A concludes the etiology of white (melancholic) and yellow (bilious) purulent eye fluxes, prescribing purgation with species dia turbith or cochia/aureae pills, shoulder/nape cupping, and venesection, followed by two eye-bag poultices ('Ein guetes Säckhel auf die augen für aitern vnd Schweren') and two distilled waters ('Ein Guetes Waser für aitern vnd Schweren der augen'). Column B gives two ointments ('Ein Guetes Sälbel für das aitern der augen'), 'Ein guetes Puluer vnd Pflaster in den süren flüß', and opens the new chapter 'Stöchen vnd drükhen der augen' (gritty/sandy sensation from hot humors, blisters, or engorged veins in the conjunctiva).
Model:        Gemini 4

Column A concludes the chapter on ocular stinging and pressing ('Stöchen vnd drükhen'), distinguishing humoral vs. sanguine causes and providing four eye-water collyria ('Ein guets Wasser für drükhen vnd Stöchen der augen', 'Ein anders Wasser...', 'Waser Von das Stöchen vnd Drükhen in augen', and 'Ein anders Guets Waser'). Column B opens 'Khizlen vnd Jeiken der augen' (ocular itching and tickling), diagnosing brain vs. blood origin by eye redness, and prescribing 'Pillule Wider das Jeiken vnd Khizlen', 'Bahung Wider das Jeiken vnd Hitzig[en]', and three soothing eye waters.
Model:        Gemini 4

Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Summary:      Recto page 132 of Wellcome Collection MS.990, divided into two columns by a vertical red rule. Contains the conclusion of an ophthalmic water recipe from the preceding page, an alternative eye-water recipe, and a treatise with multiple therapeutic and topical recipes for trichiasis ('Von den Vnrechten harn der augen Liden', i.e., ingrown or misdirected eyelashes irritating the cornea), including purgative powders, bloodletting, cupping, vesicatories, epilation, and depilatory/follicle-sealing powders.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Summary:      Early New High German medical recipes (Wellcome MS.990, p. 133, verso) describing treatment of inward-turning eyelashes ('böse Haare der Augen') by means of corrosive pastes ('Corrosiff') applied to the eyelids while the patient lies stretched out on a bench, followed by three additional corrosive recipes and a healing eyewash ('Wasser nach dem Corosiff zur Haillung').

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0105.JP2#xywh=200,220,4540,6280 | Center Rule X=2430
Summary:      Recto folio (p. 134) in a two-column layout detailing the third surgical cure for trichiasis ('Die drite Chur ist. die har sambt den fleisch Hinwegh Zue Schneiden'), involving suturing and excising the eyelid margin, followed by post-operative poultice/plaster care using egg white and a mineral/gold-marked ingredient, a warning to operate while the patient is fasting, and a powder recipe for proud flesh ('Ein Puluer Zum überigen fleisch'). The right column features a large watercolor anatomical/surgical illustration of a face with blood dripping from both eyes and a curved needle/lancet at the left eye.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_c105_1] #xywh=2450,1440,2150,2880 : Surgical illustration of eyelid incision and bleeding

Summary:      Treatise on 'growths of the eyes' ('Von den Gewächßen der augen'), describing benign/fatty eyelid tumors and their surgical excision using a suture thread, small knife, and scissors (illustrated with a man's face showing bleeding eyelid tumors pierced by threads), followed by post-operative dressing with egg white, water, and tow, and a wound-healing ointment recipe ('Ain guettes Salbel Zue den geschnidtenen augen gewächß').
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Summary:      Recto page 138 in two columns: 'Von Geschwerlein der augen gersten oder habern genand' (On small ulcers/styes of the eyes, called barleycorns or oats). Describes styes/chalazia on the upper and lower eyelids, accompanied by a large watercolor portrait of a man's face with stylized black geometric facial hair and inflamed/swollen eyelids. Followed by causes (salted thick blood and viscous phlegm), a poultice ('die Erste Khur. ain Vmbschlag'), an ointment ('Ain andere Guete Salben'), two plasters ('Ain Guettes Pflaster dargüe', 'Ain Anders'), and instructions for surgical incision if salves and plasters fail.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_c109_1] #xywh=180,1580,2200,2770 : Eye Stye / Hordeolum Portrait

Summary:      Verso page 139 in two columns: Continuation of surgical procedure for eye styes (threading with a curved needle and silk thread, incising lengthwise, pressing out fluid, dressing with egg white). Followed by a new chapter: 'Von den Waser Galln der augen. oder gewachs der augen' (On water-galls or growths of the eyes / Atheromata), with a recipe for 'Ein Sehr guette Confecto Salben' containing killed mercury, surgical excision instructions, a watercolor portrait ('Figur der Waser Gall') showing bilateral swollen eyelid cysts, and post-operative dressing with digestive ointment and mercury precipitate.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_c110_1] #xywh=2820,3350,2460,2570 : Figur der Waser Gall

PAGE / FOLIO: 140 (recto) | IIIF Canvas #111 (b18775275_MS_990_0111.JP2)
Canvas URI:   https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0111.JP2
Image API:    https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/image/b18775275_MS_990_0111.JP2/full/full/0/default.jpg (Dimensions: 5736 x 6853 px)
Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0111.JP2#xywh=200,220,4540,6280 | Center Rule X=2430
Summary:      Recto page 140 in two columns: Completion of the water-gall healing instructions, followed by a new chapter: 'Von den Zittern vnd Vippern der augen Glidern' (On trembling and twitching of the eyelids). Discusses intermittent, continuous, hereditary, and convulsive eyelid twitching and their humoral/windy causes, followed by internal and external remedies: two herbal drinks ('Ain Guets Tranckh', 'Ain anders Tranckh'), a head wash ('Ain guete haubt Waschung'), two eye waters ('Ain Guetes Waser', 'Ain anders Waser'), an eyelid salve ('Ain guets Sälbel'), a snuff powder ('Ain guets Schnupf Puluor'), and dietary/regimen warnings (avoiding solitude, late suppers, cold/moist foods, and fog).
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0120.JP2#xywh=800,240,4600,6360 | Center Rule X=3100
Summary:      Verso folio (p. 149) in two columns titled 'Von Underschiedlichen augen Sälblen' (On various eye ointments), featuring a watercolor illustration of four apothecary ointment jars on a shelf at the top of the left column. Recipes cover ointments for heated/inflamed eye pains (tutia, coral, Armenian bole, white lead, fresh unsalted butter, hematite, pearls) and in the right column ointments for eye fistulas (with copaiba balsam), pain-stilling (quince seeds, roasted apples, sugar of lead), eye ulcers, inflammation/pustules, and a cataplasm for eye inflammation.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:
  * [fig_c120_1] #xywh=830,920,2270,740 : Four Apothecary Ointment Jars

Summary:      Treatises on ocular films, spots, and blemishes (fell, fleckhen, maill der augen), especially for the poor and elderly. Includes dietary and humoral regimen (avoiding sadness, weeping, smoke, bloodletting, cold, wind, dust, pond fish, pork, dairy, waterfowl, and damp air), internal remedies (medicinal salt, herbal decoctions, purging pills), and external applications (ant-oil distillation, celandine water, gold/alumen, honey, and egg-yolk oil). Illustrated with a watercolor of a human eye showing a corneal opacity.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen

  * [fig_c121_1] #xywh=640,1130,850,530 : Fig. 1

Summary:      Collection of ophthalmic waters, powders (trisenet), and collyria for eye films and blemishes. Includes a complex eye water with pike and sheep gall, a strengthening digestive powder (trisenet), a tutia-and-malmsey collyrium aged in the sun, a sky-blue copper/vitriol water, sharp eye waters, a ripe strawberry fermentation remedy, a candle-soot insufflation, and an astrological/sympathetic dandelion root amulet dug at St. Bartholomew's Day.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Summary:      Page 153 (verso), two columns. Left column features three watercolor/ink illustrations of ophthalmic instruments (two round-headed/sponge-tipped probes and one blue-grey double-ended probe with two eyed/ringed instruments below), followed by recipes for eyes struck or bruised, 'wild flesh' (pterygium) in the eyes, and blisters/pustules forming films. Right column continues the blister/film remedy, then gives a compound eye powder ('Puluer') for failing sight or brain weakness, a remedy for films ('fell der augen'), and a hen-fat and honey ointment for spots/maculae in the eye.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0125.JP2#xywh=220,260,4500,6320 | Center Rule X=2430
Summary:      Page 154 (recto), two columns, no illustrations. Left column contains ophthalmic remedies for holding back eye fluxes (hot hard-boiled egg on the neck), obstructed eye nerves (tormentil plaster), foreign bodies in the eye (eye-pearls), pain and inflammation (roasted apple, egg-white, and Armenian bole salve), dim eyes (fennel herb), and sight lost from smallpox (pimpernel juice). Right column contains remedies for a membrane/film growing over the eyes (myrrh in white rose water), hot eyes (linden blossom water), childhood cataract (pike gall with sugar), eye films (antimony and haematite powder), weeping eyes (egg-white and salt water), and incipient cataract (coarse rose water), which continues onto Page 155.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Summary:      Page 155 (verso), two columns with illustrations in both columns. Left column finishes the cataract water from p. 154, shows three circular golden-brown lozenges/troches, and gives recipes for masticatories for weeping eyes, head-strengthening lozenges ('Haubt stärckhente Zeltel'), another lozenge for catarrhal head, and head pills for eye weakness. Right column finishes the head pills, illustrates eight conical and disc-shaped 'Sief' collyria, and gives recipes for 'Sief album Rasis', 'Sief album sine opio', 'Sief de Rosis', and 'Sief de Thure'.
Model:        Gemini 4 Hydrogen
Illustrations / Figures on Canvas:

  * [fig_c126_2] #xywh=3270,960,2140,480 : Sief collyria forms (cones and discs)

Summary:      Dietary regimen and nursing care for fever patients, illustrated with a framed watercolor of a bearded man seated at a table with food and drink. The text covers when to withhold or give food, the importance of small portions and clean preparation, forbidden and recommended foods in tertian fevers (barley, panada, almond milk, roasted apples, boiled plums, rice, borage, verjuice), and avoiding overly hot food.

Summary:      Page 183 (folio verso) contains Early New High German and Latin medical recipes for external and internal fever remedies ('Etliche Euserliche mittel Wider das fieber'), including foot plasters, sympathetic/magical remedies using a spider in a nutshell and plantain roots tied to the pulse or neck, cinquefoil leaves, celandine, ordinary fever drinks, St. Ambrose's fever potion, fever potions with blessed thistle and theriac water, and a series of fever powders and elderberry/celandine remedies. Illustrated with a pointing manicule in the upper left margin and a shaded ink-and-wash pitcher/jug beside the ordinary fever drink.

Summary:      Page 195 (verso) of Wellcome Collection MS.990 contains early modern German and Latin medical recipes for treating quartan and tertian fevers. The left column presents a complex electuary ('Die Lattwerung mach also') incorporating aromatic roots, herbs, hartshorn, coral, seeds, honey, and Peruvian bark (cinchona), followed by detailed German dosing and regimen instructions. The right column continues the regimen, warning against overindulgence after recovery, and adds four further fever remedies ('Volgen noch andere Mitl fir das 4 tägliche fieber', two entries titled 'Ein Anders', and 'Arcana fir das 4 tägliche vnd 3 tägliche fieber') using mithridatium, Peruvian bark, arcanum duplicatum, antimony, alchemical salts, laudanum, and herbal infusions. Two ink manicules appear on the page (one in the left column beside 'hirundinaria. Scorzonera. āā ℥j.' and one beneath the final red heading in the right column).

Summary:      Folio 97 verso, titled 'Von den Ungewissen fieber, oder Ungewissen kranckheit' (Of the uncertain fever, or uncertain illness), attributes epidemic or 'uncertain' fevers to divine punishment and miasmatic corruption of the air caused by unfavorable celestial constellations and planetary aspects. A large central watercolor illustration depicts a bare-chested patient sitting up in bed attended by a physician gesturing toward medicines and a crucifix on a table, while a weeping woman stands in the doorway on the left. The text below describes how poisoned air and crops transmit toxins into the body, producing diverse symptoms such as intense heat, inflammation, severe headache, unquenchable thirst, diarrhea, and loss of senses/appetite.

Red-Rule Box: https://iiif.wellcomecollection.org/presentation/b18775275/canvases/b18775275_MS_990_0169.JP2#xywh=300,300,4904,6253 | Center Rule X=2752
Summary:      A folio from a late 17th-century German medical manuscript (Wellcome MS.990, p. 398) discussing contagious fevers ('Contagios oder anfengig'). The text describes how pestilential poisons enter the body through air, food, drink, breath, stench, or fear, attacking the heart and brain. It provides preventive measures including fumigation with juniper wood, masterwort, and lovage, along with purgation, bloodletting, and several compound recipes (an electuary with theriac, Armenian bole, and alkermes; pills with myrrh, gum ammoniac, and aloes; and a 'famous poison powder' of valerian, swallowwort, polypody, lovage, angelica, and herb Paris). The final section addresses the cure of the fever, noting its severity as a divine punishment requiring repentance before natural remedies, and warning physicians that deceptive pulses and urine signs can mask the illness.
